subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Bridges That Still Stand
description: A fast breakdown of Roman Bridges That Still Stand for builders.

hook.text: Cars drive across Roman bridges in Spain every day. The bridges are over 2,000 years old and carry modern traffic.

buildup.text: The Alcántara Bridge in Spain spans the Tagus River with six arches and stands 150 feet above the water.

discovery.text: An inscription on the bridge reads: 'I have built a bridge that will last forever.' The engineer was not wrong.

twist.text: During wars, armies destroyed arches to stop enemies. Each time, the bridge was repaired and kept serving.

climax.text: Roman arch design distributes weight so efficiently that it requires no mortar. Gravity holds the stones in place.

punchline.text: A Roman engineer promised forever. Two thousand years later, he was right.

quiz.question: What makes Roman arch bridges so durable?
options: They used iron reinforcement hidden inside the stones
The arch design distributes weight so efficiently that no mortar is needed
They were built with a special type of waterproof stone
